audit.whatIsWrong: content.wants.foe[1] read "Land Searing Charge (E) to knock you into his Volcanic Rupture (W) pillar" — wrong slot and, more importantly, the mechanic runs the other way round.
audit.why: Volcanic Rupture is Ornn's Q, not his W (W is Bellows Breath). And Searing Charge does not knock the target into the pillar: Ornn charges, and if HE collides with terrain the impact creates a shockwave around him that knocks up nearby enemies. The pillar is the terrain he aims at. The counterplay is therefore positional and completely different from what was written — you do not dodge a displacement, you refuse to stand between Ornn and any wall or pillar.
audit.corrected: He charges into his own pillar or a wall; the impact shockwave knocks up whoever is next to him. Break line with the pillar before he E's.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.whys[0] credited Brittle to "Ornn's passive and Bellows Breath (W)", and spikes[3]/whys[6] described Call of the Forge God as a "double-knockup" / "two-knockup ult".
audit.why: Living Forge is item forging plus bonus resists — it applies nothing to you. Only Bellows Breath applies Brittle. And the ult's first pass deals damage, slows and applies Brittle but does NOT knock up; the knockup arrives only when Ornn recasts and charges into the elemental. A player braced for two knockups walks out of the first pass wrongly and stands still for the second.
audit.corrected: Brittle comes from Bellows Breath alone. The ult's first pass slows and Brittles; the recast is the pass that knocks up.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged zero cooldown-sequencing, and the full layer tracked only Volcanic Rupture with the vague note "Wall-knockup setup. Dodge it."
audit.why: The cooldown that decides this lane is Searing Charge at 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s — it is Ornn's only gap-closer, and against a champion who kites with Move Quick a spent E means a full fourteen seconds where Ornn simply cannot reach Teemo. Volcanic Rupture at 9s is the setup, not the threat.
audit.corrected: Poke freely in the 14s after Searing Charge is spent; treat Volcanic Rupture as the tell that he wants to charge into the pillar.

audit.why: 46.28% over 739 games; the content's Ornn-favoured early stages are consistent with a sub-50% matchup.

edits.after: Charge Searing Charge (E) into his own Volcanic Rupture (Q) pillar so the impact knocks you up, then Brittle-burst

edits.after: Bellows Breath (W) is the only thing that applies Brittle — Living Forge just gives him resists — but it wins his level-1 all-in if he reaches you.

edits.before: Ornn's Call of the Forge God (R) double-knockup is a long-range execute threat: always keep a mushroom on your escape path so his charge-up animation gives you a slowed warning and a movement-speed head start.
edits.after: Call of the Forge God's first pass slows and applies Brittle; only the recast, when Ornn charges into the elemental, knocks up. Keep a mushroom on your escape path so his charge-up gives you warning.

edits.before: You still win the split-push duel with full shroom coverage, but his teamfight R scales with his Masterwork items — avoid grouped fights or his two-knockup ult erases you.
edits.after: You still win the split-push duel with full shroom coverage, but his teamfight R scales with his Masterwork items — avoid grouped fights — the recast pass of his ult is what knocks up.

edits.after: - Ornn Searing Charge: 14s at rank 1 — his only gap-closer, and the knockup fires only if he hits terrain or his own Q pillar. Spend it and you have 14s free. - Volcanic Rupture: 9s, and it builds that pillar.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Volcanic Rupture's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Trade in the 14s after Searing Charge is spent — it is his only gap-closer. Bank small leads; if ahead, freeze and deny him the wave.

notes: I avoided asserting what Brittle actually does to the target, because Riot's ability text only says enemies "become Brittle" and the kit file's needsResearch block is empty. If Brittle upgrades Ornn's knockups into stuns, that is worth stating explicitly in this entry — but I could not confirm it from the kit files and did not want to guess at it in player-facing text.
